description: The donut chart illustrates the distribution of deceived conversations as a percentage across two levels of ambiguity—“Ambiguity 1 (Outer)” and “Ambiguity 2 (Inner)”—with each level segmented into three categories: “Deceived” (red), “Partially” (yellow), and “Not Deceived” (green). In the outer ring (Ambiguity 1), the “Deceived” category accounts for 67.6%, “Partially” for 31.6%, and “Not Deceived” for 10.5%. In the inner ring (Ambiguity 2), “Deceived” represents 57.9%, “Partially” 23.5%, and “Not Deceived” 8.8%. The chart visually emphasizes that higher ambiguity correlates with a greater proportion of fully deceived conversations, while the “Not Deceived” category remains the smallest in both rings. Percentages are labeled directly on the corresponding segments, and a dual legend on the right clarifies the color coding for each ambiguity level.
